setup: Eight real places are turned into simulation-ready scenes: six ScanNet++ rooms and two outdoor Mip-NeRF 360 captures (a garden and a park bench). Each scanned object becomes a textured mesh with a collider, is placed in the room and grounded. The scans are never used in training. PhysX provides the ground-truth motion in these scenes as well.
look_note: Rendered from above the cut walls: the scan as background, each scanned object as its textured mesh. Tiles are 432 x 224 pixels, cut from the evaluation renders.
selection_note: Seven of the 70 simulations in scanned places, picked by hand among those where NeuWorld follows PhysX; they are best cases, not typical ones. The model shown differs by clip and is named on each.

headline.text: On 70 simulations in scanned rooms, all three NeuWorld variants beat the assumption that nothing moves; the position error of NeuWorld+Reg is 57% of the no-motion error. The error is still 3.0 to 3.9 times that on the same motion families in the test set, mostly because of furniture shapes never seen in training.

pipeline_figure.caption: From posed photographs to a simulation-ready twin: SAM 3D Objects reconstructs each object, which is then placed, given a collider and grounded (Fig. 7 of the supplementary).
